title: Euclid's three steps past any list
hook: Name every prime there is. Euclid needs three moves to find one you missed.

knows: multiplying and dividing with a remainder
doesNotKnow: Euclid's argument that no finite list holds every prime

misconception: A long enough list of primes could be complete; or product + 1 must itself divide by one of the listed primes.
objective: The learner can say Euclid's three steps (multiply the list, add 1, divide) and why they end at a prime the list missed: every listed prime leaves remainder 1.

claims.source: Recomputed with node by trial division (Demo.tsx factor()); the stage uses the same trial division.

claims.text: For the lists 2, 3; 2, 3, 5; and 2 to 7, product + 1 is 7, 31 and 211, each prime and not on its list.
claims.source: Trial division up to the square root, recomputed with node (builder run 2026-10-14).

claims.text: Product + 1 leaves remainder 1 when divided by each prime on the list, so none of them divides it.
claims.source: The product is a multiple of each listed p, so product + 1 = q·p + 1 with 0 < 1 < p. Stage rows show (N − 1)/p × p and r 1; checked with node for the four lists offered.

claims.text: Product + 1 is above 1, so it has a prime factor, and that prime is not on the list.
claims.source: Its smallest divisor above 1 is prime; by c3 it is not a listed prime. Shown on the stage by 'Find its primes'.

claims.text: Any finite list gets the same three steps, so no list holds every prime.
claims.source: c3 and c4 hold for any finite list of primes. Hardy and Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers, Theorem 4.

claims.text: This is Euclid's proof in the Elements, Book IX, Proposition 20.
claims.source: Euclid, Elements IX.20 ('Prime numbers are more than any assigned multitude of prime numbers'), Heath translation; D. E. Joyce's online edition, Clark University, Book IX Proposition 20.

recall.question: Someone claims 2, 3 and 5 are all the primes. What are Euclid's three steps, and where do they end?
options: Multiply to 30, add 1 to get 31, divide: each leaves remainder 1, so 31 brings a prime not on the list
Multiply to 30, divide by 2: 30 is even, so the list is wrong
Add them to 10, add 1 to get 11, which is prime
recall.why: Product + 1 leaves remainder 1 for every listed prime, so its own prime factors (here 31 itself) are missing from the list.
